root.label: Three-way comparison
root.note: operator<=> answers ordering, operator== answers equality, and the compiler rewrites the rest.

children.label: Comparison categories
children.note: The result type of <=> says what kind of order the type has.

children.label: strong_ordering
children.note: Equal values are interchangeable; built-in for integers, enums and pointers.

children.label: weak_ordering
children.note: Equivalent values may still be distinguishable, as in case-insensitive strings.

children.label: partial_ordering
children.note: Adds unordered; built-in <=> on floating point returns it, and NaN is unordered.

children.label: One-way conversions
children.note: strong converts to weak converts to partial, never the other way.

children.label: Compare with literal 0
children.note: Test results as r < 0 or r == 0; comparing with any other value is undefined.

children.label: Built-in <=>
children.note: Applies the usual arithmetic conversions, but more strictly than <.

children.label: No narrowing
children.note: -1 <=> 1u is ill-formed because int to unsigned narrows.

children.label: Unrelated pointers
children.note: Comparing pointers into unrelated objects gives an unspecified result.

children.label: Defaulting
children.note: = default compares bases, then members, in declaration order.

children.label: Implicit ==
children.note: A defaulted <=> declares a defaulted == only if no operator== is declared.

children.label: auto return type
children.note: Deduces the common category; deleted if any member lacks <=>.

children.label: Named return type
children.note: Lets the compiler synthesize the result from == and < for legacy members.

children.label: Deleted cases
children.note: Reference members and union-like classes make defaulted comparisons deleted.

children.label: Rewritten candidates
children.note: Overload resolution adds rewritten and reversed forms for comparisons.

children.label: Relational
children.note: a < b also tries (a <=> b) < 0 and 0 < (b <=> a).

children.label: Equality
children.note: a != b tries !(a == b) and !(b == a); a == b tries b == a.

children.label: Tie-breakers
children.note: Ordinary candidates beat rewritten ones, and non-reversed beat reversed.

children.label: bool required
children.note: A rewritten == chosen for != or reversed == must return bool.

children.label: C++20 breakage
children.note: Reversed candidates appeared in old code without warning.

children.label: Non-const member ==
children.note: Normal and reversed candidates each win one argument, so C++20 calls it ambiguous.

children.label: P2468 escape hatch
children.note: A matching operator!= in the same scope stops that == from being rewritten or reversed.

children.label: No == from <=>
children.note: A hand-written <=> never provides ==, because equality can often be cheaper.

children.label: Library helpers
children.note: Function objects and exposition-only helpers built on <=>.

children.label: compare_three_way
children.note: Calls <=> and gives a strict total order over pointers.

children.label: synth-three-way
children.note: Used by pair, tuple and containers; falls back on < and yields weak_ordering.

children.label: strong_order
children.note: Gives floating point the IEEE total order, so NaNs have a place.
